– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test `testNewStringNullInput_CODEC229()` fails because calls to `StringUtils.newStringUtf8(null)` and `StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(null)` are expected to return null instead of throwing a NullPointerException (NPE). From the code snippets, the `newStringUtf8(byte[])` method calls `newString(byte[], Charset)` with the UTF-8 charset. The `newString(byte[], Charset)` method explicitly checks if the `bytes` input is null: if so, it returns null, otherwise it creates a new String with the given bytes and charset.

Therefore, `newStringUtf8(null)` returns null correctly according to this code. The same pattern can be expected for `newStringIso8859_1(null)`.

The bug report mentions that this behavior (returning null for null input) was lost with a particular fix related to using charset objects (CODEC-136).

The most plausible explanation is that the current implementation outside the snippet for `newStringIso8859_1(byte[])` and potentially other `newStringxxx` methods does not call the centralized `newString(byte[], Charset)` method with null checks, but perhaps directly invokes the `new String(bytes, charset)` constructor without null checks, causing an NPE.

The failing test shows the expectation that passing null returns null and does not cause NPE. The presence of this test and the bug report indicate that some `newStringxxx` methods may not delegate their calls properly to the safe `newString` helper method.

Hence the root cause is that some `newStringxxx` helper methods like `newStringIso8859_1()` do not perform a null check or fail to delegate to the common `newString` method that handles null safely, leading to NPE instead of null return.

No related recent bug reports are available to provide more evidence or fixes.

This explains why the test failed and the behavior is inconsistent with expectations. Fixing all `newStringxxx` methods to delegate properly to `newString(byte[], Charset)` will restore expected null-safe behavior.

---

Next, I will check the method `newStringIso8859_1(byte[])` to confirm whether it delegates correctly or not.

messages.content: "338 :     public static String newStringIso8859_1(final byte[] bytes) {\n339 :         return new String(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1);\n340 :     }"

The method `newStringIso8859_1(byte[])` directly calls `return new String(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1);` without any null check or delegating to the centralized `newString(byte[], Charset)` method.

This confirms the diagnosis: `newStringIso8859_1(null)` will throw a NullPointerException here because the `new String(bytes, charset)` constructor does not accept a null byte array.

To fix the bug and match the expected behavior, this method should delegate to `newString(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1)` which contains the required null check.

This explains why the test expecting null output fails with NPE for `newStringIso8859_1(null)`. The root cause is inconsistent null safety handling among the `newStringxxx` methods, with some like `newStringUtf8` delegating correctly and others like `newStringIso8859_1` not delegating and lacking null checks.

No relevant recent bug reports are available, so this reasoning is based purely on the test, report description, and source code inspection.
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testNewStringNullInput_CODEC229()` checks that calling `StringUtils.newStringUtf8(null)` and `StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(null)` returns null rather than throwing a NullPointerException (NPE). Inspecting `newStringUtf8(byte[])` reveals it delegates to a helper method `newString(byte[], Charset)` which checks for null and returns null accordingly, so `newStringUtf8(null)` behaves correctly.

However, `newStringIso8859_1(byte[])` does not delegate to the helper but directly calls `new String(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1)` without any null check. This causes an NPE if `bytes` is null, violating the contract expected by the test. The bug report indicates that this null safety was lost due to changes made to use Charset objects.

Hence, the bug arises because some `newStringxxx` methods do not centrally handle null input but directly use the `new String` constructor without null checks, causing NPE for null inputs. Fixing these methods to delegate to the existing null-safe helper method would restore expected null-safe behavior and pass the test.

No recent bug reports provide further clues, so this diagnosis is based on test code, bug report description, and source inspection.

Suggested fix: ensure all `newStringxxx(byte[])` variants delegate to `newString(byte[], Charset)` that handles null input correctly.

---
